source.text: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּה֙ יוֹצֵ֣ר גֹּבַ֔י בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת עֲל֣וֹת הַלָּ֑קֶשׁ וְהִ֨נֵּה־לֶ֔קֶשׁ אַחַ֖ר גִּזֵּ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, he [was] forming locusts at [the] beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was the] late crop after the mowings of the king.

en.L: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming locusts at the beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was] the late crop after the king's mowings.
en.B: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming swarms of locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up, the crop that grows after the king's share has been mown.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me a vision. He was making swarms of locusts. It was just when the second crop was starting to come up, after the king's share of the first crop had been cut.

es.L: Así me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: he aquí, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} formaba langostas al comenzar a brotar la cosecha tardía; y he aquí, [era] la cosecha tardía después de las siegas del rey.
es.B: Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba formando enjambres de langostas justo cuando comenzaba a brotar la cosecha tardía, la que crece después de que se ha segado la parte del rey.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} me mostró una visión. Él estaba haciendo enjambres de langostas. Era justo cuando la segunda cosecha empezaba a brotar, después de que se había cortado la parte de la primera cosecha que le tocaba al rey.

fr.L: Voici ce que me fit voir le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : voici, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} formait des sauterelles au début de la pousse du regain ; et voici, [c’était] le regain après les fauchaisons du roi.
fr.B: Voici ce que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} me fit voir : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} formait des essaims de sauterelles au moment où le regain commençait à pousser, le regain qui vient après qu’on a fauché la part du roi.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} m’a montré une vision. Il fabriquait des essaims de sauterelles. C’était juste au moment où la deuxième récolte commençait à pousser, après qu’on avait coupé la part de la première récolte qui revenait au roi.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha hivi: tazama, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akiumba nzige mwanzoni mwa kuchipua kwa mmea wa pili; na tazama, [ulikuwa] mmea wa pili baada ya kufyekwa kwa [majani ya] mfalme.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alichonionyesha: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akiumba makundi ya nzige wakati mmea wa pili ulipoanza kuchipua, yaani mmea unaoota baada ya fungu la mfalme kufyekwa.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha maono. Alikuwa akiumba makundi ya nzige. Ilikuwa wakati mazao ya pili yalipoanza kuchipua, baada ya fungu la mfalme la mazao ya kwanza kukatwa.

vi.L: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tạo nên đàn châu chấu vào lúc vụ mùa muộn bắt đầu mọc lên; và kìa, [đó là] vụ mùa muộn sau khi cắt cỏ cho vua.
vi.B: Đây là điều Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang tạo nên những đàn châu chấu đúng lúc vụ mùa muộn bắt đầu mọc lên, là vụ mùa mọc lên sau khi phần của vua đã được cắt.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy một khải tượng. Ngài đang tạo nên những đàn châu chấu. Đó là lúc vụ mùa thứ hai bắt đầu mọc lên, sau khi phần của vua trong vụ đầu đã được cắt.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다. 보라, 그분께서 늦게 뿌린 곡식이 자라기 시작할 때에 메뚜기를 만들고 계셨다. 보라, 그것은 왕의 몫을 벤 뒤에 [자라는] 늦은 곡식이었다.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 보여 주신 것은 이러하다. 그분께서 메뚜기 떼를 만들고 계셨다. 그때는 왕의 몫을 베어 낸 뒤에 자라는 늦은 곡식이 막 돋아나기 시작할 때였다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 환상을 보여 주셨다. 그분께서 메뚜기 떼를 만들고 계셨다. 그때는 첫 곡식 가운데서 왕의 몫을 베어 낸 뒤, 두 번째 곡식이 막 돋아나던 때였다.

pt.L: Assim o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou: eis que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava formando gafanhotos no começo da brotação da erva tardia; e eis que [era] a erva tardia, depois das ceifas do rei.
pt.B: Isto foi o que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou: {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava formando enxames de gafanhotos bem quando a erva tardia começava a brotar, a erva que cresce depois que a parte do rei já foi ceifada.
pt.R: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou uma visão. Ele estava fazendo enxames de gafanhotos. Era bem na hora em que a segunda colheita começava a brotar, depois que a parte do rei na primeira colheita já tinha sido cortada.

decisions.choice: the first of five visions
decisions.reason: Chapters 7-9 report five visions: the locusts (7:1-3), the fire (7:4-6), the plumb line (7:7-9), the basket of summer fruit (8:1-3) and the Lord beside the altar (9:1-4). The first four begin the same way, 'Thus the Lord GOD showed me'. In the first two Amos prays and the LORD relents; in the next two the LORD says that he will no longer pass by his people; in the last there is no dialogue at all. Amos tells the visions in prose, with his words and the LORD's as a conversation.

decisions.choice: the late crop after the king's mowings: the second growth of spring, after the king's share was cut
decisions.reason: Leqesh is the late growth that comes up with the spring rains. 'The king's mowings' seem to be a first cutting taken as tax, perhaps for the royal horses and herds (compare 1 Kings 18:5). The late crop was what the farmers had left for themselves and their animals; if locusts ate it, there would be nothing until the next year.

decisions.choice: locusts: swarms of locusts
decisions.reason: Gobay is a word for locusts (Nahum 3:17). A swarm could strip a land bare (Joel 1:4). The LORD is 'forming' them, the word used of a potter shaping clay: the plague is his work.

decisions.choice: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: look (L); This is what the Lord GOD showed me (B); The Lord GOD showed me a vision (R)
decisions.reason: The opening formula of the visions keeps one wording at each level in 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1. 'Look' (hinneh) is kept at Literal and left to the sense at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: swarms of; the crop that grows after (B); the second crop; of the first crop (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain what the late crop and the king's mowings were (m2).

decisions.choice: "Así me mostró el Señor DIOS: he aquí" (L); "Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor DIOS" (B); "El Señor DIOS me mostró una visión" (R)
decisions.reason: The opening of each vision (7:1, 4, 7; 8:1) keeps one wording at each level, after the Spanish vision formula of the terms note (L "he aquí").

decisions.choice: Amos's first-person account of his visions and the story of 7:10-17: passé simple at L and B ("me fit voir", "je dis", "Amatsia envoya"), passé composé at R ("m'a montré", "j'ai dit"); imparfait for what was going on in the vision
decisions.reason: Amos tells what he saw and what happened at Bethel; French written narrative uses the passé simple, and Readable the passé composé, as the term sheet sets for first-person narrative in the prophets. The words spoken inside the story keep the tenses of speech.

decisions.choice: "Bwana MUNGU alinionyesha hivi: tazama" (L); "Hiki ndicho Bwana MUNGU alichonionyesha:" (B); "Bwana MUNGU alinionyesha maono" (R)
decisions.reason: The opening of the visions (7:1, 4, 7; 8:1) keeps one wording at each level. The visions are told as narrative, so the verbs take -li- and -ka-.

decisions.choice: "Chúa là CHÚA cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa" (L), "Đây là điều Chúa là CHÚA cho tôi thấy" (B), "cho tôi thấy một khải tượng" (R)
decisions.reason: One opening per level for the visions of 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1; Amos narrates as "tôi".

decisions.choice: In the vision reports Amos narrates in the plain style with "나" and gives God -시- and "그분" ("보여 주셨다", "만들고 계셨다")
decisions.reason: The term sheet's rule for the prophets' first-person narration (Amos, Ezekiel, Zechariah).

decisions.choice: "le regain" (L, B) for the late crop
decisions.reason: French's word for the grass that grows again after a mowing, which is what the late crop is (the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Assim o Senhor DEUS me mostrou: eis que (L); Isto foi o que o Senhor DEUS me mostrou (B); O Senhor DEUS me mostrou uma visão (R)
alternatives: Assim me fez ver o Senhor DEUS
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the opening of the visions (7:1, 4, 7; 8:1) keeps one wording at each level, as the English does (m1).

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־כִּלָּה֙ לֶֽאֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ סְֽלַֽח־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said, Lord Yahweh, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.

en.L: And it happened, when they had finished eating the vegetation of the land, that I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, forgive, please! How can Jacob stand? For he [is] small."
en.B: When they had eaten up the green plants of the land, I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
en.R: The locusts ate every green plant in the land. Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive your people! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando terminaron de comer la hierba de la tierra, dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, perdona, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego! ¿Cómo podrá sostenerse Jacob? Porque es pequeño».
es.B: Cuando acabaron con la vegetación del país, dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, perdona, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Jacob? Es tan pequeño».
es.R: Las langostas se comieron todas las plantas verdes del país. Entonces dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, perdona a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Israel? Es tan pequeño y débil».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand elles eurent fini de manger l’herbe du pays, que je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, pardonne, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie ! Comment Jacob tiendra-t-il ? Car il [est] petit. »
fr.B: Quand elles eurent dévoré toute la verdure du pays, je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, pardonne, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie ! Comment Jacob pourrait-il survivre ? Il est si petit. »
fr.R: Les sauterelles ont mangé toutes les plantes vertes du pays. Alors j’ai dit : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, pardonne à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ! Comment Israël pourrait-il survivre ? Il est si petit et si faible. »

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokwisha kula mimea ya nchi, nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, samehe, tafadhali! Yakobo atawezaje kusimama? Kwa maana yeye [ni] mdogo."
sw.B: Walipokwisha kula mimea yote ya kijani ya nchi, nilisema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali samehe! Yakobo atawezaje kuishi? Yeye ni mdogo mno."
sw.R: Nzige walikula kila mmea wa kijani katika nchi. Ndipo nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali uwasamehe watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}! Israeli itawezaje kuishi? Ni ndogo na dhaifu mno."

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi chúng đã ăn hết cây cỏ trong xứ, thì tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ! Làm sao Gia-cốp đứng nổi? Vì nó [thật] nhỏ bé."
vi.B: Khi chúng đã ăn sạch cây cỏ trong xứ, tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ! Làm sao Gia-cốp tồn tại được? Nó thật nhỏ bé."
vi.R: Châu chấu ăn sạch mọi cây xanh trong xứ. Bấy giờ tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha thứ cho dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}! Làm sao Y-sơ-ra-ên sống còn được? Dân ấy thật nhỏ bé và yếu đuối."

ko.L: 그것들이 그 땅의 풀을 다 먹어 치웠을 때에 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 용서해 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 설 수 있겠습니까? 그는 작습니다."
ko.B: 메뚜기 떼가 그 땅의 푸성귀를 다 먹어 치웠을 때에 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 용서해 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 그는 너무나 작습니다."
ko.R: 메뚜기 떼가 그 땅의 푸른 풀을 모두 먹어 치웠다. 그때 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 주님의 백성을 제발 용서해 주십시오! 이스라엘이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 이스라엘은 너무 작고 약합니다."

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando eles acabaram de comer a vegetação da terra, eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, perdoa, por favor! Como Jacó se manterá de pé? Pois ele [é] pequeno."
pt.B: Quando acabaram de devorar as plantas verdes da terra, eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, perdoa, por favor! Como Jacó vai sobreviver? Ele é tão pequeno!"
pt.R: Os gafanhotos comeram todas as plantas verdes da terra. Então eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, por favor, perdoa o teu povo! Como Israel vai sobreviver? Ele é tão pequeno e fraco!"

decisions.choice: when they had finished eating: Amos prays as the locusts finish their work
alternatives: if they finished eating (a warning before it happens)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'and it was, if they finished' is unusual. It is usually read as 'when they had finished'. In the vision Amos sees the crop all but gone, and he prays before the picture becomes fact.

decisions.choice: forgive: pardon the people's sin, and so hold back the judgment
decisions.reason: Amos does not deny that the people deserve judgment; he asks the LORD to pardon them. In the second vision he asks only that the LORD stop (verse 5).

decisions.choice: How can Jacob stand? He is small: Israel is too weak to survive such a blow
decisions.reason: Amos calls the people 'Jacob', the name of their ancestor, and pleads that they are small and helpless. The rich of Samaria thought themselves 'the first of the nations' (6:1); the prophet sees how small they are before the LORD.

decisions.choice: survive (B, R); Israel; your people; small and weak (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'survive' for 'stand'. Readable says 'Israel' for 'Jacob', adds 'your people' as the object of 'forgive', and adds 'weak' to bring out what 'small' means here (m3).

decisions.choice: "de grâce" for the particle na'
decisions.reason: The plea keeps the urgency of na' without a pronoun for God that would need a setting span; 7:5 has the same wording.

decisions.choice: Amos prays in 합쇼체 with the bare vocative "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}" ("용서해 주십시오")
decisions.reason: Prophets speak to God in 합쇼체; the term sheet uses the bare name as the vocative, since "이여/여" cannot follow both forms of the span.

decisions.choice: tú to God
decisions.reason: Amos prays to God with tú, with the vocative "Señor DIOS" and no "oh", as the terms note sets for the prophets.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa là CHÚA, xin ..." with "thưa" for Amos speaking to God
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to God with "lạy" and "xin" and calls him "Ngài", as the terms sheet gives for Amos; God answers him with "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R) in 7:8 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: perdoa (tu)
decisions.reason: Amos speaks to God, so Portuguese uses "tu" at every level, as the style guide sets for anyone addressing God; Readable adds "o teu povo", as the English adds "your people". The same plea in verse 5 keeps these words.

source.text: נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh relented concerning this. It will not be, said Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning this. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented. "It will not happen," {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se retractó de esto. «No sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} desistió. «No sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cambió de parecer. «No sucederá», dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça à cela. « Cela n’arrivera pas », dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} y renonça. « Cela n’arrivera pas », dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a renoncé à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} projet. « Cela n’arrivera pas », a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý về điều này. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều ấy sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều ấy sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều ấy sẽ không xảy ra."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 일에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키셨다. "그 일은 일어나지 않을 것이다." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 뜻을 돌이키셨다. "그 일은 일어나지 않을 것이다." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 마음을 바꾸셨다. "그 일은 일어나지 않을 것이다." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} desistiu disso. "Não acontecerá", disse {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} desistiu. "Isso não vai acontecer", disse {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mudou de ideia. "Isso não vai acontecer", disse {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: relented: the LORD turned back from the judgment he had shown
decisions.reason: Nicham means to be sorry or to change one's course. It is often used of the LORD holding back a punishment he had announced (Exodus 32:14; Jeremiah 18:8; Jonah 3:10). It shows that the prophet's prayer mattered. It does not mean that the LORD had done wrong.

decisions.choice: changed his mind (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'changed his mind' for 'relented', in the sense explained in m1.

decisions.choice: "se retractó" (L); "desistió" (B); "cambió de parecer" (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting as set for the prophets (retractarse at L, Jeremiah 18:8) and as in Joel 2:13-14 here.

decisions.choice: "akaghairi" (L, B); "akabadili nia yake" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joel 2:13 and Jeremiah 18:8.

decisions.choice: "뜻을 돌이키셨다" (L, B), "마음을 바꾸셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: As Exodus 32:14 and Jonah 3:10; the LORD turns back from the judgment without having done wrong (m1).

decisions.choice: "renonça à cela" (L), "y renonça" (B), "a renoncé à son projet" (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting is "renoncer à" in the French prophets at every level; "se repentir" would suggest a fault in God.

decisions.choice: "đổi ý" at every level
decisions.reason: God relenting is "đổi ý", as in Joel 2:13 and Exodus 32:14.

decisions.choice: desistiu (L, B); mudou de ideia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is God turning from a judgment he has shown (m1). "Arrepender-se" now suggests regret for a wrong done, so Literal and Balanced say "desistir" and Readable "mudar de ideia", the words Jeremiah 4:28 sets in Portuguese for this verb. Verse 6 keeps them.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קֹרֵ֛א לָרִ֥ב בָּאֵ֖שׁ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ אֶת־תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אֶת־הַחֵֽלֶק׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, [the] Lord Yahweh [was] calling to contend by fire; and it devoured the great deep, and it was devouring the portion.

en.L: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion [of land].
en.B: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: there was the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, summoning fire to judge. It dried up the great deep and was eating up the land.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me another vision. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling for fire to punish the people. The fire dried up the deep waters under the earth and began to burn up the land.

es.L: Así me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: he aquí, el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} llamaba a juicio por medio del fuego, y [este] devoró el gran abismo y estaba devorando la porción [de tierra].
es.B: Esto es lo que me mostró el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} convocaba al fuego para juzgar. El fuego secó el gran abismo y estaba consumiendo la tierra.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} me mostró otra visión. El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} estaba llamando al fuego para castigar al pueblo. El fuego secó las aguas profundas que están debajo de la tierra y comenzó a quemar los campos.

fr.L: Voici ce que me fit voir le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : voici, le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait à plaider par le feu, et il dévora le grand abîme, et il dévorait la part [de terre].
fr.B: Voici ce que le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} me fit voir : le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait le feu pour juger. Le feu assécha le grand abîme et il dévorait le pays.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} m’a montré une autre vision. Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} appelait le feu pour punir le peuple. Le feu a asséché les eaux profondes sous la terre et il a commencé à brûler le pays.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha hivi: tazama, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiita kushindana kwa moto, nao ukakila kilindi kikuu, na ulikuwa ukilila fungu [la nchi].
sw.B: Hiki ndicho Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alichonionyesha: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiuita moto ili kuhukumu. Ulikikausha kilindi kikuu, na ulikuwa ukiila nchi.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alinionyesha maono mengine. Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} alikuwa akiuita moto ili kuwaadhibu watu. Moto huo ulikausha maji ya vilindi vilivyo chini ya ardhi, ukaanza kuiteketeza nchi.

vi.L: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa, Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi lửa đến để tranh tụng, và lửa thiêu nuốt vực sâu lớn và đang thiêu nuốt phần [đất].
vi.B: Đây là điều Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi lửa đến để xét xử. Lửa làm khô cạn vực sâu lớn và đang thiêu nuốt đất đai.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi thấy một khải tượng khác. Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang gọi lửa đến để trừng phạt dân chúng. Lửa làm khô cạn những vùng nước sâu dưới lòng đất và bắt đầu thiêu rụi đất đai.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다. 보라, 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 불로 심판하시려고 [불을] 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 큰 깊음을 삼키고, 그 몫의 [땅을] 삼키고 있었다.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 보여 주신 것은 이러하다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 심판하시려고 불을 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 큰 깊음을 말려 버리고 땅을 삼키고 있었다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나에게 또 다른 환상을 보여 주셨다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 백성을 벌하시려고 불을 부르고 계셨다. 그 불이 땅 밑의 깊은 물을 말려 버리고 땅을 태우기 시작했다.

pt.L: Assim o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou: eis que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} estava chamando para julgar pelo fogo, e ele devorou o grande abismo e estava devorando a porção [de terra].
pt.B: Isto foi o que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou: lá estava o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, chamando o fogo para julgar. O fogo secou o grande abismo e estava devorando a terra.
pt.R: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} me mostrou outra visão. O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} estava chamando o fogo para castigar o povo. O fogo secou as águas profundas que ficam debaixo da terra e começou a queimar a terra.

decisions.choice: calling to contend by fire: summoning fire to carry out his case against Israel
alternatives: calling for a rain of fire (dividing the letters as lirvivei 'esh)
decisions.reason: Riv is a legal case, and the LORD calls for fire to carry out his judgment (compare Isaiah 66:16). The phrase 'to contend by fire' is unusual, and some divide the letters differently to read 'calling for a shower of fire'. The sense is close either way: a fire of judgment sent by the LORD.

decisions.choice: the great deep: the waters under the earth that feed springs and rivers
decisions.reason: Tehom rabbah is the great deep, the waters below the earth (Genesis 7:11; Isaiah 51:10). This fire is so fierce that it dries up the sources of water, and then it begins on the land.

decisions.choice: the portion: the land given to Israel as its share
decisions.reason: Cheleq is a share or allotted portion, here the farmland divided among Israel's families (Micah 2:4). The fire is eating up the land itself.

decisions.choice: summoning fire to judge (B); to punish the people (R); dried up; the land (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'the land' for 'the portion' (m3) and 'dried up' for what fire does to water. Readable explains 'the great deep' (m2) and says what the fire is for.

decisions.choice: chamando para julgar pelo fogo
decisions.reason: The noun is a legal case (m1); Portuguese "julgar" says it plainly where "contender" is archaic.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ חֲדַל־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Lord Yahweh, cease, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.

en.L: And I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, cease, please! How can Jacob stand? For he [is] small."
en.B: Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please stop! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
en.R: Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please stop! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

es.L: Y dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, cesa, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego! ¿Cómo podrá sostenerse Jacob? Porque es pequeño».
es.B: Entonces dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, detente, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Jacob? Es tan pequeño».
es.R: Entonces dije: «¡Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, detente, por favor! ¿Cómo podrá sobrevivir Israel? Es tan pequeño y débil».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, arrête, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie ! Comment Jacob tiendra-t-il ? Car il [est] petit. »
fr.B: Alors je dis : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, arrête, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie ! Comment Jacob pourrait-il survivre ? Il est si petit. »
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit : « Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, arrête ! Comment Israël pourrait-il survivre ? Il est si petit et si faible. »

sw.L: Nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, acha, tafadhali! Yakobo atawezaje kusimama? Kwa maana yeye [ni] mdogo."
sw.B: Ndipo nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali acha! Yakobo atawezaje kuishi? Yeye ni mdogo mno."
sw.R: Ndipo nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, tafadhali acha! Israeli itawezaje kuishi? Ni ndogo na dhaifu mno."

vi.L: Và tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin ngừng lại! Làm sao Gia-cốp đứng nổi? Vì nó [thật] nhỏ bé."
vi.B: Bấy giờ tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin ngừng tay! Làm sao Gia-cốp tồn tại được? Nó thật nhỏ bé."
vi.R: Bấy giờ tôi thưa: "Lạy Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin ngừng tay! Làm sao Y-sơ-ra-ên sống còn được? Dân ấy thật nhỏ bé và yếu đuối."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 멈추어 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 설 수 있겠습니까? 그는 작습니다."
ko.B: 그래서 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 멈추어 주십시오! 야곱이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 그는 너무나 작습니다."
ko.R: 그래서 내가 말했다. "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 제발 멈추어 주십시오! 이스라엘이 어떻게 살아남겠습니까? 이스라엘은 너무 작고 약합니다."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, para, por favor! Como Jacó se manterá de pé? Pois ele [é] pequeno."
pt.B: Então eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, para, por favor! Como Jacó vai sobreviver? Ele é tão pequeno!"
pt.R: Então eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, por favor, para! Como Israel vai sobreviver? Ele é tão pequeno e fraco!"

decisions.choice: cease: Amos now asks only that the LORD hold back
decisions.reason: In verse 2 Amos asked the LORD to forgive; now he asks only that he stop. The rest of the plea repeats verse 2 word for word, and the wording here repeats it at each level.

source.text: נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את גַּם־הִיא֙ לֹ֣א תִֽהְיֶ֔ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh relented concerning this. Also it will not be, said [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning this. "This also will not happen," said the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented. "This will not happen either," the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} said.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind again. "This will not happen either," said the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se retractó de esto. «Tampoco esto sucederá», dijo el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} desistió. «Esto tampoco sucederá», dijo el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} volvió a cambiar de parecer. «Esto tampoco sucederá», dijo el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça à cela. « Cela non plus n’arrivera pas », dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} y renonça. « Cela non plus n’arrivera pas », dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a encore renoncé à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} projet. « Cela non plus n’arrivera pas », a dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi kuhusu jambo hili. "Hili nalo halitatukia," Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} akasema.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi. "Hili nalo halitatukia," Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} akasema.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tena. "Hili nalo halitatukia," Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} akasema.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý về điều này. Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều này cũng sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều này cũng sẽ không xảy ra."
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lại đổi ý. Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Điều này cũng sẽ không xảy ra."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 일에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키셨다. "이 일도 일어나지 않을 것이다." 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 뜻을 돌이키셨다. "이 일도 일어나지 않을 것이다." 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다시 마음을 바꾸셨다. "이 일도 일어나지 않을 것이다." 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} desistiu disso. "Também isto não acontecerá", disse o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} desistiu. "Isto também não vai acontecer", disse o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mudou de ideia outra vez. "Isto também não vai acontecer", disse o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD relents again, as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The LORD answers as in verse 3, now with 'also'. Twice the prophet's prayer holds back judgment. In the next two visions he does not pray, and the LORD says that he will not pass by his people again (7:8; 8:2).

source.text: כֹּ֣ה הִרְאַ֔נִי וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲדֹנָ֛י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־חוֹמַ֣ת אֲנָ֑ךְ וּבְיָד֖וֹ אֲנָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus he showed me, and look, [the] Lord [was] standing on a wall of plumb line, and in his hand a plumb line.

en.L: Thus {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed me: look, the Lord was standing beside a wall [built with] a plumb line, with a plumb line in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.
en.B: This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall built true to a plumb line, with a plumb line in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.
en.R: Then the Lord showed me another vision. He was standing beside a wall that had been built straight, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was holding a plumb line.

es.L: Así me mostró: he aquí, el Señor estaba de pie junto a un muro hecho a plomada, con una plomada en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano.
es.B: Esto es lo que me mostró: el Señor estaba de pie junto a un muro hecho a plomada, con una plomada en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano.
es.R: Luego el Señor me mostró otra visión. Estaba de pie junto a un muro construido bien derecho, y tenía en la mano una plomada.

fr.L: Voici ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me fit voir : voici, le Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} tenait près d’un mur [bâti au] fil à plomb, avec un fil à plomb dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main.
fr.B: Voici ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me fit voir : le Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} tenait près d’un mur bien d’aplomb, un fil à plomb à la main.
fr.R: Ensuite, le Seigneur m’a montré une autre vision. Il {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} tenait près d’un mur qui avait été bâti bien droit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tenait un fil à plomb.

sw.L: Alinionyesha hivi: tazama, Bwana alikuwa amesimama kando ya ukuta [uliojengwa kwa] timazi, na timazi mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho alichonionyesha: Bwana alikuwa amesimama kando ya ukuta uliojengwa sawasawa kwa timazi, akiwa na timazi mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.R: Kisha Bwana alinionyesha maono mengine. Alikuwa amesimama kando ya ukuta uliojengwa wima, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alikuwa ameshika timazi.

vi.L: Ngài đã cho tôi thấy thế này: kìa, Chúa đang đứng bên một bức tường [xây theo] dây dọi, tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm một dây dọi.
vi.B: Đây là điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho tôi thấy: Chúa đang đứng bên một bức tường được xây ngay theo dây dọi, tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm một dây dọi.
vi.R: Rồi Chúa cho tôi thấy một khải tượng khác. Ngài đang đứng bên một bức tường được xây thẳng, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm một dây dọi.

ko.L: 그분께서 나에게 이와 같이 보여 주셨다. 보라, 주님께서 다림줄로 [쌓은] 성벽 곁에 서 계셨고, 그분의 손에는 다림줄이 있었다.

decisions.choice: 'anakh: a plumb line, a weight of lead or tin hung on a cord
alternatives: tin: a wall of tin, and tin in his hand
decisions.reason: The word 'anakh is found only in verses 7-8. It has long been understood as a plumb line, a weight hung on a cord to test whether a wall is straight. In Akkadian, a related language, the word means tin, and some take the vision to show the Lord holding tin: perhaps a picture of weapons, or of a wall that cannot stand, or a play on a word for groaning. The plumb line fits verse 8 best: the LORD will test his people as a builder tests a wall, and a crooked wall comes down (compare 2 Kings 21:13; Isaiah 28:17).

decisions.choice: the Lord was standing: Amos sees the Lord himself in this vision
decisions.reason: In the first two visions Amos was shown what the Lord was doing; here he sees the Lord himself, standing beside the wall. The usual words 'the Lord GOD' are shortened to 'he' and 'the Lord'.

decisions.choice: built true to a plumb line (B); built straight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what 'a wall of a plumb line' means: a wall built straight, checked with a plumb line (m1). Readable names the Lord at the start, since 'he' alone would be unclear.

decisions.choice: "plomada" at every level; "un muro hecho a plomada" (L, B), "un muro construido bien derecho" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets, after 2 Kings 21:13 in Spanish. The Hebrew 'anakh may mean tin, as the meaning footnote says; the Spanish keeps one word for the tool.

decisions.reason: The term sheet's word, as the French 2 Kings 21:13; the English meaning decision notes the other reading, "tin".

decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 21:13 and Isaiah 28:17. The English notes that the Hebrew word may mean tin.

decisions.choice: "dây dọi" at every level
decisions.reason: 'Anakh is "plumb line", the published "dây dọi" of 2 Kings 21:13; the meaning decision footnotes "tin" as another reading.

decisions.choice: *'Anakh* is "다림줄" at every level; *Adonai* alone is "주님"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word (Isaiah 28:17; 2 Kings 21:13); the footnote gives "tin". Readable keeps the image, as the English does.

decisions.choice: um prumo (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: 'anakh (m1) is "prumo" at every level, as the English keeps "plumb line": the builder's weight on a cord, which Brazilians know by that word. The reading "tin" is left to the meaning note.

en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "What do you see, Amos?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am placing a plumb line among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "I am going to test {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel with a plumb line, to see whether they are straight. I will not let them go unpunished any longer.

decisions.choice: setting a plumb line in the midst of my people: testing Israel and finding it crooked
decisions.reason: A builder holds a plumb line against a wall to see whether it is straight, and a wall that leans has to be pulled down. The LORD is testing his people by his standard, and verse 9 gives the result.

decisions.choice: I will not pass by them again: I will no longer spare them
decisions.reason: To pass by someone is to overlook their wrong and spare them (Micah 7:18; Proverbs 19:11). In the first two visions the LORD relented; now he says he will not spare them again. 8:2 repeats the line. Compare 5:17, where he will pass through their midst to judge them.

decisions.choice: test ... to see whether they are straight; let them go unpunished (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what setting a plumb line among the people means (m1) and what 'pass by' means (m2).

decisions.choice: "plus jamais je ne passerai outre" (L), "Je ne fermerai plus les yeux sur ses fautes" (B), "Je ne le laisserai plus sans punition" (R)
alternatives: "je ne passerai plus à côté de lui"
decisions.reason: To pass by someone is to spare him (m2); "passer outre" keeps the verb "passer" with the sense of overlooking. 8:2 repeats the wording.

decisions.choice: God to Amos: "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R); Amos: "tôi thưa"
decisions.reason: The address settled for God speaking to the prophets in these books; 8:2 follows it.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Amos in 해라체 ("아모스야, … 보느냐?"); Amos answers in 합쇼체 ("다림줄입니다")
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address forms for God and the prophets.

decisions.choice: "ya no volveré a pasarle por alto" (L); "Ya no se lo dejaré pasar más" (B); "Ya no dejaré más tiempo sin castigo" (R)
decisions.reason: "Pass by" means "spare"; L keeps the picture, B and R say the sense. The Lord's words run into verse 9, so the « » closes there.

decisions.choice: O que vês, Amós? (tu)
decisions.reason: God speaks to one person with "tu", as the Old Testament notes set it; the same question returns in 8:2.

decisions.choice: nunca mais passarei por ele (L); Não vou mais deixar passar (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of passing by; Balanced says "deixar passar", the Portuguese idiom for letting a wrong go unpunished, which is the sense (m2). Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: the high places of Isaac: hilltop shrines, named after Israel's ancestor Isaac
decisions.reason: Bamot were open-air shrines, often on hills. Only Amos calls Israel 'Isaac' (also verse 16). The name may point to Beersheba, which was linked with Isaac (5:5; 8:14; Genesis 26:23-25), or simply to the people as Isaac's descendants.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam: the royal family of Jeroboam II
decisions.reason: Jeroboam II was king of Israel when Amos prophesied (1:1). His son Zechariah reigned only six months before he was murdered, and with him the family's rule ended (2 Kings 15:8-10).

decisions.choice: hilltop places where Isaac's people worship; King Jeroboam's family (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the high places were and who 'Isaac' is (m1), and that the house of Jeroboam is the king's family (m2).

decisions.choice: "los lugares altos" (L, B), "los santuarios en las colinas" (R)

decisions.choice: a story set among the visions
decisions.reason: Verses 10-17 tell, in prose, how the priest of Bethel tried to silence Amos. The story follows the third vision because that vision ends with the sword against the house of Jeroboam (verse 9), the words Amaziah reports to the king (verse 11). It is the only story about Amos in the book, and it speaks of him in the third person.

decisions.choice: Amaziah the priest of Bethel: the chief priest of the royal shrine
decisions.reason: Bethel was the king's sanctuary (verse 13), set up by Jeroboam I (1 Kings 12:28-33). Amaziah is known only from this passage.

decisions.choice: conspired: plotted rebellion; the land cannot bear his words
decisions.reason: Qashar is the word for a political plot against a king (2 Kings 15:10). Amaziah presents Amos's words as treason. The land 'cannot bear' them, as a vessel cannot hold more than it can contain.

decisions.choice: "Amatsia, prêtre de Béthel"
decisions.reason: The form the term sheet sets for the Twelve, from the French Kings' Amatsia; the king's dialogue partners say "tu" to the king, as in Kings.

decisions.choice: "A-ma-xia, thầy tế lễ ở Bê-tên"
decisions.reason: The terms-sheet name and title; Amaziah speaks to the king as a subject ("vua") and of Amos as "ông ta".

decisions.choice: Amaziah's report to the king is 합쇼체 with "임금님"; to Amos he speaks hostile 해라체 ("선견자야, 가거라", 7:12), and Amos answers in 해라체
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address forms for Amos and Amaziah.

decisions.choice: "Amasías"
decisions.reason: The priest's name in the form Spanish gives the king of Judah of the same name (2 Kings 14).

decisions.choice: Amazias, o sacerdote de Betel; contra o senhor (to the king)
decisions.reason: The priest is "Amazias", the form the name has for the king of Judah in 2 Kings 14 in Portuguese. He writes to the king, so Portuguese addresses Jeroboam as "o senhor", the form for speaking to a superior (style guide section 4).

decisions.choice: Jeroboam will die by the sword: Amaziah sharpens verse 9

decisions.choice: seer: a prophet, perhaps said with scorn

decisions.choice: eat bread there: make your living there
decisions.reason: Amaziah assumes that Amos prophesies for pay, as professional prophets did (Micah 3:5, 11), and tells him to go and earn it in his own country. Amos came from Tekoa in Judah (1:1).

decisions.choice: you prophet; Go back; Earn your living there by prophesying (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'prophet' for 'seer', 'go back' for 'flee', since Amos came from Judah, and joins the last two commands to show what Amaziah means (m2).

decisions.choice: "Voyant, va-t'en" (L); "Va-t'en, toi le voyant !" (B); "Va-t'en d'ici, toi le prophète !" (R)

decisions.choice: "Hỡi kẻ tiên kiến" at every level, with "ông" between the two men

decisions.choice: hostile 해라체: "선견자야, 가거라"

decisions.choice: vidente; você (vá, fuja)

decisions.choice: I am not a prophet, nor a prophet's son: Amos denies being a professional prophet
alternatives: I was not a prophet, nor a prophet's son (until the LORD called me)
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses no verb here, so the sentence can be read in the present ('I am not') or the past ('I was not'). In the present, Amos refuses Amaziah's picture of him as a prophet who earns his bread by prophesying (verse 12): he is not one of the professionals. In the past, he means that he was not a prophet until the LORD took him from the flock (verse 15). Either way, he prophesies because the LORD sent him, not because it is his trade; in verse 15 the LORD himself tells him to 'prophesy'.

decisions.choice: a son of a prophet: a member of a company of prophets
decisions.reason: 'Sons of the prophets' were groups of prophets who lived and worked together, often under a leader such as Elisha (2 Kings 2:3; 4:38). 'Son' here means a member or disciple, not a child. Amos says that he never belonged to such a group.

decisions.choice: a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs
decisions.reason: Boqer is one who keeps cattle (baqar). In 1:1 Amos is called one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, and in verse 15 the LORD took him 'from following the flock'. The sycamore fig is a kind of fig tree that grew in the warm lowlands (1 Kings 10:27). Its fruit had to be slit or pinched while growing so that it would ripen and be sweet, and boles seems to name that work. Amos may have owned flocks and orchards or worked for others; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a member of a company of prophets (B); trained as a prophet; raise livestock; fig trees (R)
decisions.reason: Ben-navi' is 'a son of a prophet' at Literal, 'a member of a company of prophets' at Balanced and 'trained as a prophet' at Readable, as 2 Kings 2:3 and the terms note settle (m2). Readable says 'I was not trained' for the present 'I am not a son of a prophet', which comes to the same thing. It says 'raise livestock' for 'herdsman' and 'fig trees' for 'sycamore figs'.

decisions.reason: Ben-navi' takes the terms-sheet wording at each level, as 2 Kings 2:3.

decisions.reason: "Filho de profeta" at Literal and "grupo de profetas" at Balanced keep the words 2 Kings 2:3 gives the sons of the prophets in Portuguese (m2). "Boiadeiro" is one who keeps cattle (m3); "sicômoros" is the word 1 Kings 10:27 uses for the sycamore fig, and Readable says "figueiras", as 1 Kings does.

decisions.choice: took me from following the flock: as the LORD took David
decisions.reason: The LORD says of David, 'I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep' (2 Samuel 7:8; compare Psalm 78:70-71). Amos's authority does not come from a group of prophets or from a shrine, but from the LORD's call.

decisions.choice: my people Israel: the LORD still calls them his people
decisions.reason: Even when he sends Amos with words of judgment, the LORD calls Israel 'my people' (7:8; 8:2).

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level ("m'a pris", "m'a dit")
decisions.reason: Amos is speaking to Amatsia, so his account of his call keeps the tenses of speech, not the passé simple of the narrative around it.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֗ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תַטִּ֖יף עַל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And now hear the word of Yahweh. You [are] saying, You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip against the house of Isaac.

en.B: So now hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and stop preaching against the house of Isaac.'
en.R: Now listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel. Stop preaching against the people of Isaac.'

ko.L: 그러니 이제 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 들어라. 너는 '이스라엘을 치는 예언을 하지 말고, 이삭의 집을 치는 [말을] 떨어뜨리지 말아라' 하고 말한다.

ko.R: 이제 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀을 들어라. 너는 나에게 '이스라엘에 대하여 예언하지 마라. 이삭의 자손에게 설교하지 마라' 하고 말한다.

pt.L: E agora ouça a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Você está dizendo: 'Não profetizarás contra Israel, e não gotejarás [palavras] contra a casa de Isaque.'
pt.B: Agora, pois, ouça a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Você me diz: 'Não profetize contra Israel e pare de pregar contra a casa de Isaque.'
pt.R: Agora escute o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz. Você me diz: 'Não profetize contra Israel. Pare de pregar contra o povo de Isaque.'

decisions.choice: drip words: preach, let words fall like drops
decisions.reason: Hittif, 'to drip', is used of speaking or preaching (Micah 2:6, 11; Ezekiel 21:2). It may carry a note of scorn, like 'drivel'.

decisions.choice: you say: Amos quotes Amaziah's order back to him
decisions.reason: Amaziah's words of verse 13 are given again in a sharper form, now as the very thing for which judgment will come. Israel and the house of Isaac are the same people (verse 9).

decisions.choice: preaching (B, R); the people of Isaac (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1). Readable says 'people' for 'house'.

decisions.choice: "dejar caer [palabras]" (L); "predicar" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "drip" of speech is kept as a picture at L, with the supplied word bracketed; B and R say what it means.

decisions.choice: não gotejarás [palavras]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of words falling in drops (m1), with the commands in the future of the Hebrew prohibition; Balanced and Readable say "pregar".

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֞ בָּעִ֤יר תִּזְנֶה֙ וּבָנֶ֤יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְאַדְמָתְךָ֖ בַּחֶ֣בֶל תְּחֻלָּ֑ק וְאַתָּ֗ה עַל־אֲדָמָ֤ה טְמֵאָה֙ תָּמ֔וּת וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land by a measuring line will be divided, and you on unclean ground will die, and Israel will surely go into exile from upon its land.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land will be divided up by measuring line; and you yourself will die on unclean ground, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Your wife will be made a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be struck down by the sword, and your land will be measured out and divided. You yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from its land.'"
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Your wife will have to become a prostitute in the city. Your sons and daughters will be killed by the sword. Your land will be measured and divided up among others. You yourself will die in a foreign land, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not worshiped. And the people of Israel will surely be taken from their land as captives.'"

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Tu mujer será prostituta en la ciudad, y tus hijos y tus hijas caerán a espada, y tu tierra será repartida a cordel; y tú mismo morirás en tierra inmunda, e Israel ciertamente irá al destierro lejos de su tierra”».
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: “Tu mujer será prostituida en la ciudad, tus hijos y tus hijas caerán a espada, y tu tierra será medida y repartida. Tú mismo morirás en una tierra impura, e Israel ciertamente irá al destierro, lejos de su tierra”».
es.R: Así que esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Tu esposa tendrá que hacerse prostituta en la ciudad. Tus hijos y tus hijas morirán a espada. Tu tierra será medida y repartida entre otros. Tú mismo morirás en una tierra extranjera, donde no se adora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y el pueblo de Israel será llevado prisionero lejos de su tierra”».

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Ta femme se prostituera dans la ville, et tes fils et tes filles tomberont par l’épée, et ta terre sera partagée au cordeau ; et toi, tu mourras sur une terre impure, et Israël ira sûrement en exil loin de sa terre.” »
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : “Ta femme sera prostituée dans la ville, tes fils et tes filles tomberont par l’épée, et ta terre sera mesurée et partagée. Toi-même, tu mourras sur une terre impure, et Israël ira certainement en exil, loin de sa terre.” »
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Ta femme devra se prostituer dans la ville. Tes fils et tes filles seront tués par l’épée. Ta terre sera mesurée et partagée entre d’autres. Toi-même, tu mourras dans un pays étranger, où l’on n’adore pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et le peuple d’Israël sera sûrement emmené captif loin de sa terre.” »

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: 'Mke wako atakuwa kahaba mjini, na wana wako na binti zako wataanguka kwa upanga, na nchi yako itagawanywa kwa kamba ya kupimia; nawe mwenyewe utakufa katika nchi najisi, na hakika Israeli watakwenda uhamishoni mbali na nchi yao.'"
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: 'Mke wako atafanywa kahaba mjini, wana wako na binti zako watauawa kwa upanga, na nchi yako itapimwa na kugawanywa. Wewe mwenyewe utakufa katika nchi najisi, na hakika Israeli watapelekwa uhamishoni, mbali na nchi yao.'"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: 'Mke wako atalazimika kuwa kahaba mjini. Wana wako na binti zako watauawa kwa upanga. Nchi yako itapimwa na kugawanywa kwa watu wengine. Wewe mwenyewe utafia katika nchi ya kigeni, ambako {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haabudiwi. Na hakika watu wa Israeli watachukuliwa mateka kutoka katika nchi yao.'"

vi.L: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: 'Vợ ông sẽ làm gái mại dâm trong thành, con trai và con gái ông sẽ ngã dưới gươm, đất của ông sẽ bị chia bằng dây đo; còn chính ông sẽ chết trên đất ô uế, và Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị lưu đày khỏi đất của mình.'"
vi.B: Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: 'Vợ ông sẽ bị bắt làm gái mại dâm trong thành, con trai và con gái ông sẽ bị gươm giết, đất của ông sẽ bị đo đạc và chia cho người khác. Còn chính ông sẽ chết nơi đất ô uế, và Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị lưu đày khỏi đất của mình.'"
vi.R: Vì vậy, đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: 'Vợ ông sẽ phải làm gái mại dâm trong thành. Con trai và con gái ông sẽ bị gươm giết. Đất của ông sẽ bị đo đạc và chia cho người khác. Còn chính ông sẽ chết ở một xứ ngoại bang, nơi người ta không thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên chắc chắn sẽ bị bắt làm phu tù, đem đi khỏi đất của họ.'"

ko.L: 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 창녀 노릇을 하고, 네 아들들과 네 딸들은 칼에 쓰러지며, 네 땅은 측량줄로 나뉠 것이다. 그리고 너는 부정한 땅에서 죽고, 이스라엘은 반드시 자기 땅에서 떠나 사로잡혀 갈 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 몸을 팔게 되고, 네 아들딸들은 칼에 맞아 쓰러지며, 네 땅은 측량되어 나뉠 것이다. 너는 부정한 땅에서 죽고, 이스라엘은 틀림없이 자기 땅에서 쫓겨나 사로잡혀 갈 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. '네 아내는 성읍에서 몸을 팔 수밖에 없게 될 것이다. 네 아들딸들은 칼에 맞아 죽을 것이다. 네 땅은 측량되어 다른 사람들에게 나뉠 것이다. 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기지 않는 이방 땅에서 죽을 것이다. 그리고 이스라엘 백성은 틀림없이 포로가 되어 자기 땅에서 끌려갈 것이다.'"

pt.L: Por isso assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'A sua mulher será prostituta na cidade, e os seus filhos e as suas filhas cairão pela espada, e a sua terra será repartida a corda de medir; e você mesmo morrerá em terra impura, e Israel certamente irá para o exílio, para longe da sua terra.'"
pt.B: Por isso assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'A sua mulher será feita prostituta na cidade, os seus filhos e as suas filhas serão mortos à espada, e a sua terra será medida e repartida. Você mesmo morrerá numa terra impura, e Israel com certeza será levado para o exílio, para longe da sua terra.'"
pt.R: Por isso, é isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: 'A sua mulher vai ter de se tornar prostituta na cidade. Os seus filhos e as suas filhas vão ser mortos à espada. A sua terra vai ser medida e repartida entre outros. Você mesmo vai morrer numa terra estrangeira, onde {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} não é adorado. E o povo de Israel com certeza vai ser levado da sua terra como prisioneiro.'"

decisions.choice: the fate of a conquered city
decisions.reason: Each line names what happened when a city fell: women were taken by the soldiers or left to support themselves by prostitution, the young were killed, and the land was measured out for new owners (Micah 2:4-5). Amaziah himself would die in exile.

decisions.choice: unclean ground: a foreign land
decisions.reason: Israel's land belonged to the LORD. Any other land was unclean, because other gods were worshiped there and its food was not dedicated to the LORD (Hosea 9:3-4; Ezekiel 4:13). A priest, whose life was bound up with what is clean and unclean, would die in such a place.

decisions.choice: Israel will surely go into exile: Amos repeats the words Amaziah reported
decisions.reason: Amos does not take back the words Amaziah complained of (verse 11); he repeats them word for word, as the LORD's sentence.

decisions.choice: be a prostitute (L); be made a prostitute (B); have to become a prostitute (R)
decisions.reason: Here zanah is used of real prostitution, not of Israel's unfaithfulness to God, so the wording settled for Hosea ('prostitute oneself', 'be unfaithful') is not used. Balanced says 'be made' and Readable 'have to', since in a conquered city it would be forced on her (m1).

decisions.choice: among others; a foreign land, where the LORD is not worshiped (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who will get the land (m1) and what 'unclean ground' means (m2).

decisions.choice: "será prostituta" (L); "será prostituida" (B); "tendrá que hacerse prostituta" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution is said plainly, as the English decision for Amos 7:17 sets; the verb zanah of Israel's unfaithfulness is not meant here.

decisions.choice: "se prostituera" (L), "sera prostituée" (B), "devra se prostituer" (R)
decisions.reason: Here prostitution is literal, the fate of a conquered city, so French says it plainly, as the term sheet asks for zanah in this sense.

decisions.choice: "atakuwa kahaba" (L); "atafanywa kahaba" (B); "atalazimika kuwa kahaba" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution is said plainly ("kahaba"), as the term sheet sets; "kufanya ukahaba" is kept for Israel's unfaithfulness to God.

decisions.choice: "làm gái mại dâm" (L); "bị bắt làm gái mại dâm" (B); "phải làm gái mại dâm" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal prostitution is "làm gái mại dâm", as the terms sheet says for this verse, kept apart from "làm điếm" for Israel's unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: Literal prostitution is "창녀 노릇을 하다" (L) and "몸을 팔다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "음행하다" for Israel's unfaithfulness to God and says literal prostitution plainly.

decisions.choice: a sua mulher; você mesmo
decisions.reason: The LORD's sentence is spoken through Amos to Amaziah, a man, and comes inside Amos's own words to him, so Portuguese keeps the "você" of verse 16 rather than turning to "tu".
